standard.title: Multiplication facts for twos
standard.description: recall and demonstrate proficiency with multiplication facts for twos; extend and apply facts to develop the related division facts using doubling and halving
standard.prior_knowledge: Students quantify sets by skip counting (AC9M1N03) and solve sharing/grouping problems (AC9M1N06). They have not yet connected skip counting in twos to multiplication facts or established doubling and halving as inverse operations.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recall multiplication facts for twos with proficiency and extend and apply those facts to derive related division facts using doubling and halving.

nodes.label: Doubling as multiplication by 2
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can double numbers within 20 using materials or mental strategies and connect doubling to multiplying by 2.
nodes.minimum_width: Double at least five numbers within 20 using materials; connect to 'multiply by 2' language.
nodes.typical_width: Double numbers within 20 using physical and virtual materials; recognise the relationship between double, twice and multiply by 2; use a hundreds chart to colour doubles and identify the pattern.
wider: Use doubling to establish near doubles: if double 5 is 10, then double 6 is 10+2=12; extend to double 4 is 10-2=8
Investigate doubling patterns on a hundreds chart; describe the pattern of even numbers produced
success_criteria: Doubles numbers within 20 correctly using materials or mental strategy
Explains that 'double 6', 'twice 6' and '6 multiplied by 2' mean the same thing

nodes.label: Recall of twos multiplication facts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recall multiplication facts for twos (2×1 through 2×10) with fluency.
nodes.minimum_width: Recall twos multiplication facts within 2×10 without reconstructing by counting; respond promptly when presented with random facts.
nodes.typical_width: Recall all twos multiplication facts fluently; recognise that 2×8 = 8×2 (commutativity); apply to find related facts (e.g. 8 twos uses the same fact as 2 eights).
wider: Limited width — multiplication fact recall for twos is a fluency skill that does not vary meaningfully across contexts. Extension involves applying known twos facts to derive other facts (e.g. 4×3 = double 2×3) or connecting to related division facts, addressed in node 3.
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 3 requires students to derive division facts from known multiplication facts under the inverse relationship. Students still reconstructing twos facts by counting cannot hold the part-whole structure in working memory simultaneously — fluency at Node 2 is the prerequisite.

response_modes.reason: Fluency with twos facts requires practise volume. Games and repeated oral/written practice across different formats build automaticity that supports later work on other multiplication tables.

success_criteria: Recalls twos multiplication facts within 2×10 correctly
Responds to randomly ordered twos facts without counting

nodes.label: Halving as division by 2
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can halve numbers within 20 and connect halving to dividing by 2, deriving related division facts from known multiplication facts.
nodes.minimum_width: Halve at least four even numbers within 20 using materials; state the related division fact.
nodes.typical_width: Halve numbers within 20; connect to 'divide by 2' language; derive related division facts from multiplication facts (e.g. 2×7=14, so 14÷2=7); practise doubling and halving games.
wider: Use a doubling and halving game (e.g. virtual dice: choose to double or halve to reach a target number); apply known facts strategically
Investigate: 'If I know 2×9=18, what else do I know?' — list all related facts including division

response_modes.reason: The inverse relationship between multiplication and division — like that between addition and subtraction — requires explicit reasoning scaffold. Students need to see that 'if 2 groups of 7 make 14, then 14 shared into groups of 2 gives 7' before they can derive division facts independently.

success_criteria: States the related division fact for a given twos multiplication fact
Explains why doubling and halving are inverse operations
